steps.text: Thread your needle with one strand of 3364 and outline the grassy mound using split stitch. Then fill the outer ring of the mound with long and short stitch, angling your rows to follow the curve of the ground.
Switch to 470 and fill the inner oval of the mound with long and short stitch, blending into the previous colour so the two greens merge naturally where they meet.

Using 904, embroider the grass blades on the left with rows of split stitch, following each blade from base to tip. Fill the two leaves on the right with satin stitch, angling the stitches out from the stem like the veins of a real leaf.
Now fill in the four small dots around the mound with french knots using two strands of 986. Wind the thread around your needle twice for a nice plump knot.
Using Ecru, fill the petals of the little flower on the left with satin stitch, working each petal from the outside edge in towards the centre.
Complete the flower by filling its centre with a small cluster of french knots in 3821. The flora is now complete - time to move on to the toadstool itself!

Outline the stem with split stitch in Ecru, then fill it with vertical rows of long and short stitch, working from the top of the stem downwards. Keep your stitch direction parallel to the sides of the stem.
Use 3047 to add the shaded side of the stem and the underside of the skirt. Blend this colour into the Ecru you have already stitched - this shadow is what gives the stem its roundness.
Fill the dark band underneath the cap with 3777 using satin stitch, keeping the stitches vertical. This dark edge anchors the cap and makes the red really glow above it.

Outline the bottom edge of the cap with split stitch in 3830, then fill the lower band of the cap with long and short stitch. Curve your rows to follow the rim of the cap, stitching around the white spots as you reach them.

Fill the top of the cap with 608, blending down into the previous row of 3830. Work in rows that follow the dome of the cap and let the longer stitches fight into each other's rows - this is where the cap gets its rounded, glowing look.

Finally, fill each of the white spots on the cap with satin stitch in Ecru. Angle the stitches in one consistent direction per spot, and use split stitch around larger spots first for a crisp raised edge. Your toadstool is complete - give yourself a pat on the back!
